topics.title: Spatial Information Technology and GIS
topics.ncert_sections: What is Spatial Information Technology?; What is GIS?; Forms of Geographical Information

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of spatial information and the technologies that make up Spatial Information Technology.
Define GIS and explain how it goes beyond database management and computer assisted cartography to support decisions.
Distinguish spatial data (positional, linear and areal) from non-spatial or attribute data.

topics.title: Sources of Spatial Data and Advantages of GIS
topics.ncert_sections: Forms of Geographical Information; Advantages of GIS over Manual Methods

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways spatial data are built in a GIS core and the factors governing the choice of a data source.
State the characteristics of topographical and thematic maps that make them a source of spatial data.
Evaluate the advantages of GIS over manual methods of map making and analysis.
Identify the five components of GIS and the role of each.
Relate GIS operations to the functional modules of GIS application software.

topics.title: Spatial Data Formats: Raster and Vector

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how raster data represent features as grid cells and how cell size affects resolution.
Describe how vector data represent features through coordinate pairs of points.
Compare the advantages, disadvantages and typical uses of raster and vector formats.

topics.title: Sequence of GIS Activities and Spatial Data Input
topics.ncert_sections: Sequence of GIS Activities; Spatial Data Input; Scanners

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange the activities involved in GIS-related work in their correct sequence.
Explain the compatibility checks needed when digital data sets from different suppliers are combined.
Explain how scanners convert analogue maps into digital raster images.

topics.title: Attribute Data, Verification, Editing and Conversion
topics.ncert_sections: Entering the Attribute Data; Data Verification and Editing; Data Conversion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify attribute data of spatial entities and the sources from which they are entered into GIS.
Identify common errors in captured spatial data and the methods used to verify and correct them.
Explain why and how data are converted between vector and raster formats.
Explain why spatial and attribute data sets must be correctly linked in GIS.
Explain exact matching of files through a common key.
Distinguish hierarchical matching from fuzzy matching and choose the right one for a given data set.

topics.title: Spatial Analysis: Overlay and Buffer Operations
topics.ncert_sections: Spatial Analysis; Overlay Analysis Operations; Buffer Operation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain overlay analysis and its use in studying land use change and urban sprawl.
Apply buffer operations to proximity analysis of facilities and pollution sources.
